❯ Without using any tools, write about 600 words of plain prose on the history of canals.                                                                                                               

⏺ Canals are among the oldest large engineering works, and for most of recorded history they were a practical answer to two problems: getting water where people needed it, and moving heavy goods more
  cheaply than land allowed. Their story runs from the irrigation ditches of early river civilizations to the ship canals that changed global trade.

  The first canals were built for water, not boats. In Mesopotamia, farmers between the Tigris and Euphrates dug channels as early as the sixth millennium BCE to carry river water onto dry fields.
